# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# A REFERENCE ERROR SHAPE, NOT A SERVED FIXTURE. The mock dispatches on the wire method name, and
# `error-not-open` is not a method, so this file is never selected by a request. It exists to pin the
# shape and the exact message, and to be the source of the --fail argument that produces it:
#     fmonero-mock --role wallet --fail get_height=-13:'No wallet file'
# THE CODE AND MESSAGE ARE UPSTREAM'S, VERBATIM: wallet_rpc_server::not_open sets
#     er.code = WALLET_RPC_ERROR_CODE_NOT_OPEN;  er.message = "No wallet file";
# (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:480-485), and the code is -13
# (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_error_codes.h:46). The message is "No wallet file" -- three words, no
# trailing period, and NOT "no wallet open" or "Wallet is not open". A test that matches on prose must
# match this string.
# NOTE the envelope below has NO "jsonrpc" and NO "id" key, unlike node/error-restricted.json. That is
# deliberate and is what DESIGN.md §8 Phase 0 specifies for this file: it pins the `error` OBJECT,
# because the envelope around it is built by the mock (and by epee) from the request's own id. A
# consumer parses error.code and error.message.
# -13 IS NOT AN ERROR IN THE ONE PLACE IT MATTERS MOST (§5, §5b): the hot-path wallet `get_height` is
# simultaneously the reachability probe AND the open/closed probe, so -13 means "reachable AND no
# wallet open" -- status.wallet.reachable is TRUE, status.wallet.open is false, and status exits 0
# with the wallet_closed info warning. Only a TRANSPORT error means unreachable.
# EVERYWHERE ELSE -13 MAPS TO EXIT 9 wallet_locked (§1b.4), with the hint `fmonero wallet open <name>`.
# It also reaches fmonero from on_set_daemon called with no wallet loaded (:4692) -- see
# set_daemon.json for why that ordering trap exists.
